Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 59, verse 1:

Naming of the Surah

• It is called al-Hashr (The Gathering/Exile), because its opening mentions the expulsion of the Jews of Banu al-Nadir from their dwellings adjacent to Madinah, so they dispersed to Khaybar and the lands of al-Sham. That was their first expulsion from the Arabian Peninsula.

Among the Objectives of the Surah

• To show the signs of God's power and the manifestations of His might and His support for the Prophet (ﷺ), through the expulsion of the Jews of Banu al-Nadir from their homes and homeland, despite the fortresses and strongholds they had, and to explain a number of rulings concerning fay' (property taken from the enemy without battle).

• To exalt the standing of the Companions of the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and to highlight the virtues of the Muhajirun (Emigrants) and the Ansar (Helpers), and of those who came after them among the sincere believers who love them.

• To mention a number of the characteristics of the hypocrites, and to expose the evil of their intentions, and to show the similarity between the hypocrites' deceiving the Jews with promises of support and Satan's deceiving those who disbelieve, so that the outcome for all of them is eternal abiding in the Fire.

• To admonish the believers by commanding them to be mindful of God (taqwa) and by reminding them of the Day of Resurrection, to explain the difference between the people of Paradise and the people of the Fire, to highlight the greatness and majesty of the Qur'an, and to conclude by mentioning a number of God's Beautiful Names, which indicate God's greatness, perfection, and transcendence above every deficiency.

[The Tafsir]

Everything in the heavens and everything on the earth glorifies God, exalting Him above all that is unfitting for Him. He is the Mighty, whom none can overpower, the Wise in His decree, His management, His creation, and His legislation, who places things in their proper places.

He is the One who expelled those among the People of the Book who denied the prophethood of Muhammad (ﷺ), namely the Jews of Banu al-Nadir, from their homes which were adjacent to the Muslims around "al-Madinah." This was the first expulsion of them from the "Arabian Peninsula" to "al-Sham" (Greater Syria). You, O Muslims, did not think that they would leave their homes in such humiliation and disgrace, because of the severity of their might and the strength of their fortresses. The Jews thought that their fortresses would protect them from the punishment of Allah, and that no one could overcome them. But there came upon them a decree from Allah that they had never imagined, and Allah cast terror and intense dread into their hearts. They were destroying their own homes with their own hands and with the hands of the believers. So take heed, O people of sound insight and sharp intellect, from what happened to them.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 59, verse 3:

And had it not been that Allah had decreed for them the exile from their homes and ordained it, He would have punished them in this world with killing and captivity. And for them in the Hereafter is the punishment of the Fire.

That (what befell the Jews in this world, and what awaits them in the Hereafter) is because they opposed the command of Allah and the command of His Messenger with the utmost opposition, fought against them both, and strove in disobedience to them. And whoever opposes Allah and His Messenger, then indeed Allah is severe in punishment toward him.

Whatever palm trees you (believers) cut down, or left standing on their roots, that was by the permission of Allah and His command, so that He might humiliate the defiant transgressors who disobeyed His command and prohibition, since He empowered you to cut down their palm trees and burn them.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 59, verse 6:

"And what Allah granted as fay' (spoils returned) to His Messenger from the wealth of the Jews of Banu al-Nadir, you did not make any horses or camels charge for obtaining it. But Allah gives His messengers power over whomever He wills of His enemies, so they surrender to them without fighting. The fay': what is taken from the wealth of the disbelievers by right, without fighting. And Allah is over all things capable; nothing can overwhelm Him."

Whatever Allah has returned to His Messenger from the property of the polytheists of the towns, without any cavalry or camel being driven against them, belongs to Allah and to the Messenger. It is spent on the general welfare of the Muslims, and on the near kin of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), namely the Banu Hashim and the Banu al-Muttalib; on orphans, meaning the poor children whose fathers died while they were below the age of puberty; on the needy, meaning the people in want who do not own what suffices them and meets their need; and on the wayfarer (ibn al-sabil), meaning the stranger traveling whose provision has run out and whose wealth has been cut off from him. This is so that wealth does not circulate only among the rich, while the poor and the needy are deprived of it. And whatever the Messenger gives you of property, or whatever he prescribes for you of law, take it; and whatever he forbids you from taking or doing, abstain from it. Fear Allah by carrying out His commands and avoiding His prohibitions. Indeed Allah is severe in punishment toward whoever disobeys Him and opposes His command and prohibition. This verse is a foundation for the obligation of acting upon the Sunnah (sunnah, the prophetic practice): in speech, in action, or in tacit approval.

Likewise, the wealth that Allah has returned (as fay') to His Messenger is to be given to the poor emigrants (al-muhajirun), who were forced out of their homes and their property by the disbelievers of Makkah, seeking from Allah that He bestow upon them provision in this world and His pleasure in the Hereafter, and who support the religion of Allah and His Messenger through jihad in the way of Allah. Those are the truthful ones, who have confirmed their words by their deeds.

The commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 59, verse 9:

And those who had settled in "al-Madinah" and had believed before the migration of the emigrants—they are the Ansar—love those who emigrated to them, share their wealth with them, and do not find in their hearts any envy toward them for what they were given of the spoils (fay') and other than it. They give preference to the emigrants and the needy over themselves, even though they themselves were in need and poverty. And whoever is saved from stinginess and from withholding excess wealth, those are the successful ones, who have attained what they sought.

The Noble Qur'an, as interpreted in the King Fahd Complex commentary (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar), on surah 59, verse 10:

"And those who came after them say: 'Our Lord, forgive us and our brethren who preceded us in faith, and do not put in our hearts any resentment toward those who believe. Our Lord, You are Most Compassionate, Most Merciful.'"

Translation of the commentary:

The verse indicates that a Muslim should remember his predecessors with goodness, supplicate for them, love the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), mention them with goodness, and seek Allah's pleasure for them (taraḍḍī).

Have you not considered the hypocrites, who say to their brothers in disbelief among the People of the Book, the Jews of Banu al-Nadir: "If you are expelled, we will surely leave with you, and we will never obey anyone concerning you, and if you are fought, we will surely support you"? And Allah bears witness that they are liars in what they promised the Jews of Banu al-Nadir.

If the Jews are expelled from Madinah, the hypocrites will not go out with them. And if they are fought, the hypocrites will not fight alongside them, as they had promised. And if the hypocrites do fight alongside them, they will turn their backs and flee in defeat. Then Allah will not help them; rather, He will forsake them and humiliate them.

Surely their fear and dread of you, O believers, is greater and more intense in their hearts than their fear of Allah. That is because they are a people who do not comprehend the greatness of Allah and faith in Him, nor do they dread His punishment.

The Jews will not fight you as a united force except within fortified towns or from behind walls. Their courage fails them, and the terror that has taken hold of their hearts keeps them from facing you openly. Their enmity among themselves is fierce: you think they are united, but their hearts are divided. That is because they are a people who do not comprehend the command of Allah, nor do they reflect upon His signs.

The likeness of these Jews, in the punishment of Allah that befell them, is like that of the disbelievers of Quraysh on the day of Badr, and the Jews of Banu Qaynuqa', for they tasted the evil consequence of their disbelief and their enmity toward the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in this world. And for them in the Hereafter is a painful, afflicting punishment.

The likeness of these hypocrites, in inciting the Jews to fight and promising them victory over the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), is like the likeness of Satan when he made disbelief seem attractive to the human being and invited him to it. Then, when he disbelieved, Satan said: "I am free of you; I fear Allah, the Lord of all creatures."

The outcome for Satan and for the human being who obeyed him and so disbelieved is that both of them are in the Fire, abiding therein forever. That is the recompense of the transgressors who exceed the limits of Allah.

O you who have believed Allah and His Messenger and acted by His law, fear Allah and beware of His punishment by doing what He has commanded you and leaving what He has forbidden you. Let every soul look to what it has sent forward for the Day of Resurrection, and fear Allah in everything you do and everything you leave undone. Indeed, Allah is All-Aware of what you do; nothing of your deeds is hidden from Him, and He will recompense you for them.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 59, verse 19:

"And do not be, O believers, like those who forgot Allah, so He made them forget themselves. Those are the defiantly disobedient."

Note: The translation below renders the commentary text itself.

Do not be, O believers, like those who abandoned fulfilling the right of Allah that He had made obligatory upon them, so He caused them to forget, because of that, the shares of their own souls in the good deeds that would save them from the punishment of the Day of Resurgence. Those are the ones described as defiantly disobedient (fasiq), those who have stepped outside obedience to Allah and obedience to His Messenger.

The companions of the Fire, who are tormented, and the companions of Paradise, who are blessed with delight, are not equal. The companions of Paradise are those who attain every desired thing and are saved from every disliked thing.

Had We sent down this Qur'an upon a mountain, you would have seen it humbled and split apart out of fear of God, Exalted is He, though it is so strong, so hard and so massive, if it could comprehend what is in it of promise and threat. And these are the parables We set forth for people, making them clear, so that they may reflect upon the power and greatness of God. And in the verse there is an exhortation to contemplate the Qur'an, to understand its meanings, and to act upon it.

He is Allah, glorified and exalted, the one truly worthy of worship, besides whom there is no deity. He knows the hidden and the manifest; He knows what is absent and what is present. He is the Most Merciful (al-Rahman), whose mercy encompasses everything, and the Most Compassionate (al-Rahim) toward those among the people of faith in Him.

He is Allah, the One truly worthy of worship, besides whom there is no deity. The King of all things, who disposes of them without any hindrance or opposition; the One free of every imperfection, who is safe from every defect; the One who confirms His messengers and prophets in what He sent them with of clear signs; the Watcher over all His creation in their deeds; the Mighty who cannot be overcome; the Compeller (al-Jabbar) who has subdued all the servants, and to whom all creation submits; the Supreme (al-Mutakabbir) to whom belong greatness and majesty. Allah, exalted is He, above everything they associate with Him in worship.

He is Allah, glorified and exalted, the Creator who determines (the creation), the Originator (al-Bari') who brings them into being according to the requirements of His wisdom, the Fashioner (al-Musawwir) who shapes His creation however He wills. To Him belong the Most Beautiful Names and the Lofty Attributes. All that is in the heavens and the earth glorifies Him, and He is the Almighty (al-'Aziz), the Severe in Retribution against His enemies, the All-Wise in His management of the affairs of His creation.
